lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For Fiscal 2026, our most significant customer relationships included three Power segment customers, which accounted for approximately 23%, 16% and 11% of consolidated revenues.
For Fiscal 2025, our most significant customer relationships included three Power segment customers, which accounted for 28%, 13% and 10% of consolidated revenues.
No other customer of this reportable segment represented greater than 10% of consolidated revenues for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 or Fiscal 2024.

The revenues of our Industrial segment were $167.6 million, $167.6 million, and $142.8 million for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025, and Fiscal 2024, respectively, representing approximately 17.7%, 19.2%, and 24.9% of our consolidated revenues for the corresponding fiscal years.

Teledata segment revenues were $20.6 million, $13.5 million and $14.3 million for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025, and Fiscal 2024, respectively, representing approximately 2.2%, 1.5%, and 2.5% of our consolidated revenues for the corresponding fiscal years.
Most of our consolidated revenues are generated by the Power segment, which represented 80.1%, 79.3% and 72.6% of consolidated revenues for Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, respectively.
The revenues of this business represented approximately 80.1% of consolidated revenues for Fiscal 2026 and 79.3% of consolidated revenues for the prior fiscal year.
The revenues of this business represented approximately 17.7% of consolidated revenues for Fiscal 2026 and 19.2% of consolidated revenues for the prior fiscal year.

For Fiscal 2026, consolidated gross profit was $193.7 million, representing a gross profit percentage of approximately 20.5% of consolidated revenues, compared with $141.0 million, or approximately 16.1% of consolidated revenues, for Fiscal 2025.
Selling, general and administrative expenses were $59.0 million for Fiscal 2026 and $52.8 million for Fiscal 2025, representing 6.2% and 6.0% of consolidated revenues, respectively.
For Fiscal 2026, the Company’s most significant customer relationships included three Power customers, which accounted for 23 %, 16 % and 11 % of consolidated revenues.
For Fiscal 2025, the Company’s most significant customer relationships included three Power customers, which accounted for 28 %, 13 % and 10 % of consolidated revenues.
For Fiscal 2024, the Company’s most significant customer relationships included three Power customers which accounted for 19 %, 16 % and 15 % of consolidated revenues.

Although our contracts with certain customers include provisions intended to provide limited relief from some of these risks, the effectiveness of such protection may depend on factors outside our control, including the financial condition of our customers.

The ultimate impact of natural disasters, human-made disasters, or other catastrophic events depends on the severity, duration, and geographic scope of the event, as well as its effects on customers, supply chains, labor availability, and broader economic conditions.

In many regions, the economic viability of new generation projects depends on the expected margin between wholesale electricity prices and the cost of fuel and operations, commonly referred to as the spark spread.
The commencement and execution of projects performed by our Power segment depend on obtaining numerous regulatory approvals, including environmental, construction, and operating permits.
The development of new natural gas-fired power plants may also depend on the availability of fuel supply, which in some cases requires the construction of new natural gas pipelines.
Our continued success depends on our ability to attract, hire and retain talented personnel.

We rely on subcontractors to perform portions of our construction work and on third-party manufacturers and suppliers to provide significant equipment and materials necessary to complete our projects.
The use of cash could reduce our financial flexibility, and our ability to raise additional capital may depend on market conditions, our operating results, and other factors outside our control.
The timing and amount of any repurchases will depend on market and business conditions, applicable legal and credit requirements, and other corporate considerations.
Natural gas remains the primary source of utility-scale electricity generation in the United States and continues to play a central role in maintaining grid reliability.

As a result, project developers and utilities often rely on a relatively small group of contractors with demonstrated experience in the engineering and construction of large-scale power generation facilities.

The accuracy of our revenues and profit recognition in any period depends on the accuracy of our estimates of the forecasted contract value, or transaction price, and the cost to complete the work for each project.
